skill_classification.target_skill: Claude Agent SDK — full expertise in primitives, architecture, testing, observability, integration with Claude Code ecosystem and Postgres/AGE/pgvector, plus a system for tracking rapid SDK evolution
skill_classification.classification_notes: Primary cognitive_higher: architectural reasoning, tradeoff evaluation, design decisions for agent systems. Secondary cognitive_lower: API surface memorization, configuration patterns, tool schemas. Environment is mostly_kind because SDK behavior is deterministic and testable, but agent behavior at runtime introduces ambiguity. Tacit knowledge is moderate — best practices for prompt engineering within agents, debugging emergent agent behaviors, and knowing when to use which primitive involve pattern recognition built through practice.

related_experience.description: Expert-level Python — primary language for backend, data, and systems work
~8 hours daily for approximately a year. Deep familiarity with Claude Code CLI, plugins, skills, ~/.claude configuration, prompt engineering patterns
Heavy user of ecosystem plugins, has customized plugins and skills. Understands the skill/plugin abstraction layer sitting on top of the Agent SDK
Prior experience with competing agent framework — provides mental models for agent orchestration, tool use, state management, and graph-based workflows
Production database experience with graph (AGE) and vector (pgvector) extensions — key integration target for agent systems
Strong backend and data systems background with some full-stack projects

frameworks_and_vocabulary: Claude API concepts: messages, tools, system prompts, streaming
MCP (Model Context Protocol) — tool servers, resources
Claude Code internals: ~/.claude config, CLAUDE.md, hooks, permissions
Graph data modeling (AGE/property graphs) and vector similarity (pgvector)
Software architecture patterns: modularity, observability, testability

constraints.equipment_access: Full development environment, Claude Pro/API access, existing Postgres stack
constraints.environment_notes: Learning while actively building portfolio projects — can immediately apply new knowledge to real codebases

learner_profile.purpose: Develop deep expertise in the Claude Agent SDK to power portfolio projects, integrate with Postgres/AGE/pgvector stack, and build a systematic process for staying current as the SDK evolves rapidly. Serve as an informed architect who can evaluate tradeoffs for developers, stakeholders, and users.

approach_strategy.approach_rationale: The learner's goal requires architectural reasoning, tradeoff evaluation, and integration design — not just API surface knowledge. Whole-task 4C/ID is the right fit because: (1) they need to work with the full agent lifecycle from day one (not isolated components), (2) their existing LangChain/Claude Code experience means they can handle complex tasks early with scaffolding, (3) the integration with their database stack demands systems-level thinking that only emerges in whole-task practice. The heavy transfer potential from their existing experience means we can start at high complexity with selective scaffolding rather than building from basics.
approach_strategy.short_term_plan_summary: In 2-3 weeks, you'll have: (1) Mastery of all SDK primitives — agents, tools, handoffs, guardrails, tracing, context management — with clear mental models for when/why to use each. (2) A working integration pattern for Agent SDK ↔ Postgres/AGE/pgvector that you can replicate across projects. (3) A testing and observability framework for your agents — structured approaches to unit testing tool calls, integration testing agent flows, and monitoring production behavior. (4) A personal 'SDK changelog radar' system — a repeatable process for tracking SDK releases, evaluating breaking changes, and integrating new features. (5) Architectural fluency to explain tradeoffs to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
approach_strategy.extended_roadmap_summary: Beyond the initial sprint: (1) Contribute to the ecosystem — build and publish plugins/tools that leverage your deep understanding. (2) Multi-agent orchestration patterns — complex workflows with agent handoffs, shared state, and error recovery. (3) Performance optimization — token efficiency, latency reduction, cost modeling for production agent systems. (4) Advanced observability — custom tracing, anomaly detection in agent behavior, A/B testing agent configurations.
domain_specific_adaptations: SDK is evolving rapidly — the curriculum must include meta-skills for tracking changes, not just current-state knowledge. We'll build a 'changelog radar' workflow early.
Heavy emphasis on code-based learning — every concept gets implemented in a real project context, not just studied abstractly.
Integration-first: your Postgres/AGE/pgvector stack is the integration target throughout, so exercises build toward real architectural patterns you'll reuse.
Contrast with LangChain/LangGraph throughout — leverage your existing mental models by explicitly mapping 'in LangChain this was X, in Agent SDK it's Y and here's why'.
Claude Code ecosystem context: connect SDK primitives to the plugin/skill/hook layer you already know well, showing how they compose.
Observability and testing treated as first-class topics, not afterthoughts — given your explicit goal of improving these.

identity_frame.identity_statement: You're becoming a Claude Agent SDK architect — someone who doesn't just use the SDK but understands its design philosophy, evaluates its tradeoffs, and builds systems that evolve with it.
identity_frame.purpose_connection: This connects directly to your portfolio projects and your role as someone who bridges deep technical implementation with architectural decision-making for stakeholders. You're building the expertise to be the person teams turn to when they need to know how to build, test, and scale agent systems on Claude.
